title: Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) production trait, a useful screening to select endophytic and rhizosphere competent bacteria for rice growth promoting agents
author: Etesami, Alikhani, et al.

steps.title: Collect rhizosphere soil and roots
steps.instruction: Gather rhizosphere soil and root samples from healthy plants grown in rotation with rice at the flowering stage, selecting random locations across the field.

steps.title: Isolate and store bacterial strains
steps.instruction: Isolate endophytic and rhizosphere bacteria from the collected samples using established methods, group phenotypically similar isolates, and store all isolates at 4 °C for later use.

steps.title: Screen isolates for PGP traits
steps.instruction: Test each bacterial isolate for the four plant‑growth‑promoting (PGP) traits: indole‑3‑acetic acid (IAA) production, siderophore production, 1‑aminocyclopropane‑1‑carboxylate (ACC) deaminase activity, and phosphate solubilization.

steps.title: Test antagonism among isolates
steps.instruction: Perform an in‑vitro antagonistic assay on all isolates to identify strains that do not inhibit each other.

substeps.instruction: Conduct the assay separately for four groups of PGPR: IAA‑producing isolates, ACC deaminase‑producing isolates, siderophore‑producing isolates, and phosphate‑solubilizing isolates.
Select isolates within each group that show no antagonistic effect toward one another and retain the same PGP trait.

steps.title: Inoculate mixed strains on rice seedlings
steps.instruction: Apply mixtures of non‑antagonistic isolates (sharing the same PGP trait) to rice seedlings grown in sterile Hoagland’s medium containing 8 mM (NH₄)₂SO₄ under aseptic in‑vitro conditions and incubate for 20 days.

substeps.instruction: Prepare sterile Hoagland’s medium supplemented with 8 mM (NH₄)₂SO₄.
Mix the selected isolates that lack antagonism and share the same PGP trait.
Verify that rice seeds are free of any endophytic bacteria before inoculation.
Surface‑sterilize seeds and maintain strict aseptic technique throughout the procedure.
Inoculate the seedling roots with the bacterial mixture.
Incubate the inoculated seedlings for 20 days.
After incubation, re‑isolate the inoculated bacteria from the seedlings to confirm colonization (Koch’s postulate) and assess infection and persistence characteristics.

steps.title: Recover bacteria from seedlings after incubation
steps.instruction: After the 20‑day growth period, isolate endophytic and rhizoplane bacterial strains that have colonized the rice seedlings.

steps.title: Rescreen recovered isolates for PGP traits
steps.instruction: Evaluate the recovered endophytic and rhizoplane isolates for the same four PGP traits (IAA production, siderophore production, ACC deaminase activity, phosphate solubilization).

steps.title: Inoculate single strains on rice seedlings
steps.instruction: Inoculate each individual isolate (IAA‑producing, siderophore‑producing, ACC deaminase‑producing, or phosphate‑solubilizing) as a single‑strain treatment on rice seedlings in sterile Hoagland’s medium with 8 mM (NH₄)₂SO₄, maintain aseptic in‑vitro conditions, and grow for 20 days to assess colonization and growth‑promotion potential.

substeps.instruction: Prepare sterile Hoagland’s medium with 8 mM (NH₄)₂SO₄.
Inoculate rice seedlings with a single bacterial strain per treatment.
Incubate under the same aseptic, in‑vitro conditions for 20 days.

steps.title: Select best colonizing and growth‑promoting isolate
steps.instruction: Compare all isolates based on their ability to colonize rice roots and to enhance seedling growth (shoot biomass, root length, etc.) and identify the most effective strain.
